reviews.comment: He doesn't write the exams anymore and they are significantly harder than physics 1. DO NOT TAKE!!!
He's super funny, and he makes physics easy. Attendance isn't mandatory ,but class is super helpful for seeing problems similar to the exam! Took him for both physics 201 and 202 and got As!

Professor Ford teaches this class as if everyone in the room has prior knowledge of the content he covers and mumbles through lectures by rapidly reading off of chapter notes scribbled in sharpie. Everything I learnt in this class I had to teach to myself. I'm sure I would have enjoyed learning physics much more with another professor.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He mumbles a lot in lectures so you can hardly understand him. I never understood his lectures and they really didn't help me at all. I ended up using all the previous exams as study material and just memorized the format of what the exams looked like and what questions I should expect and did well from that.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Take this class with him. Majority of questions on the exams are exactly like the practice exams. If a few do not match, there are similar examples in his sharpie notes. Genuinely he is a caring professor and very easily accessible if you go to this office hours. The lab and recitation are very easy as well.
didn't learn anything from his lectures, but isn't too hard overall

By far the best physics prof I could have. Very knowledgeable and good sense of humor. Super easy lab, recitations are free if you attend, and homeworks are not too hard. Exams similar to last 5 years' practice exams - do them and you will be fine. VERY responsive over email outside of class and is willing to help. Highly recommend taking Ford!!

Not the best, not the worst. Go to class if u have doubts. Material might need to be self-taught. Good amount of resources (old exams, SI, and HW). He was nice and cleared any questions u have. Would definitely recommend for those who have taken phy before
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Genuinely one of the worst professors at TAMU. He couldn't even teach vectors properly, let alone anything more complicated. His handwriting is atrocious and just mumbles through the lecture. Only pro is that he gives 5 practice tests that mostly resemble what the actual test looks like. If you take him you will end up teaching yourself everything.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really nice guy who wants you to do well, but no one in physics at tamu can teach. Get A plus tutoring and teach it to yourself and you will be fine. Exams account for 80% of your grade, so that sucks, but the previous exams are exactly like the ones you get which is nice. Homework is a lot and hard so just use chat.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolutely be prepared to teach yourself the material, went to almost every lecture, and it was thoroughly unhelpful in preparing for exams. Soso much homework to keep up with (at least 2 hours per week). Nice guy overall, but if you have a difficult time teaching yourself, be prepared to struggle.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Physics is hard and this prof can't really teach the material effectively. The best thing about him is his practice exams but even then it isn't a sure fire way to do well in the class. I would recommend someone who is better at teaching the material or finding a good substitute for class (personally I used Pearson+ and it was ok)

Beware of the sharpie notes, you will either love them or hate them. The content itself isn't that hard when he gets into the practice problems. There will be like three or so homework assignments a week, but they typically do not take that long. The exams are not super hard when he writes them, but they do count for a lot of your grade. He's funny
can't explain well, exam days have 10x more people than people who go to his lecture

Going into this class I had no prior knowledge of physics and professor like Ford is not good for people who are similar to me. If it wasn't for the SI sessions I definitely would've dropped so definitely attend those to do well. Many practice exams were provided for every exam and the final so that was also my saving grace.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Physics is difficult for me, and unfortunately this class made me dislike the subject more. Dr Ford does not explain anything in class, just mumbles and half-solves random HW problems. Probably 2/3rds of the students stopped attending lectures after week 2. The amazing class SI taught me everything I learned by the end. Take someone else to learn.

Take him BECAUSE his final is better than other profs. Boring lecturer so I went to (max) 5 of his lectures (do SI). DEF solve atleast 3 yrs of his past papers before exams as the exams are very similar (including final). Beware, our exam 3 was not by Ford. Ez Free marks from Lab and recitation. HW hard so get help (chegg or chatgpt)
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's sweet but it was impossible to pay attention. Old exams are the saving grace and if you study by them you should be able to do well, but be prepared to teach yourself the content. If I had relied just on lecture Im sure I would've failed. lowest test grade gets averaged with your final. lab, homework and recitation should boost your garde.

ford is terrible at explaining, so i stopped going to class two weeks into the semester. however, he provides ALL the old exams for practice so i just powered thru the 5 most recent exams by using his notes and google for help. old exams are VERY similar to his actual exams, so just study those well. course is graded by 5 exams, hw, and lab.

I suck at physics so take this how you want. I studied so much for every exam (i did all the past exams he had which date to 2014) and i have NEVER passed a single exam. They are so hard. Rumor is he doesn't write his exams anymore. He is a nice guy, he answers emails fast and he is super sweet but he teaches you NOTHING. Be prepared for tutoring.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is easy, as he will say many times. They pretty much give you the exams beforehand that you can practice on. If you do 2-3 of the practice exams before the actual exam and memorize the questions, it may be time consuming, but you will make an A. Its a little test heavy, but Lab, Homework, and Recitation can bring you up a free 20%

He's nice but his lectures are not helpful and his teaching style did not work for me (he tends to mumble through lectures). SI sessions and recitation taught me way more and saved my grade. Read the notes posted on canvas, do the practice exams, and go to recitation and SI sessions. The exams are very similar to the practice exams.

Dr. Ford's lectures aren't great, but they are sufficient. He offers notes that can easily be followed to understand material/lectures. He offers about 10 past exams per exam, which tend to be very similar to each other. If you understand the principles behind past questions, you will be fine. He is also VERY responsive to questions over email.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Had him for 201 & 202. STUDY OLD EXAMS! He's the main writer but sometimes they switch so DON'T stick to them too much. My first couple exams were low Cs but getting A in class is still DOABLE! Lectures are pointless, try to understand the concepts, recitations are very helpful. You will NOT enjoy his class, good option if you just need an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Solid prof. Tests are very similar to old exams and he gives plenty so study them had. Cutoff point is around 85 and the lowest grade was replaced by the average of itself & the finals. Lectures are boring but he's quirky sometimes. I'm not great w physics but still got a low A.Overall, this might be your best option at College station.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Physics is horrible but Dr. Ford makes it somewhat doable. Exams are like old exams which he gives us. Replaces lowest exam grade with your final. Solid prof.

Dr. Ford is a good professor. While he isn't great with tech and his lectures are dull/slow, he is readily available to answer questions, and he writes all but one of the exams. The exams are easy and pretty similar to old practice exams, which he gives many of. Put the work in and an A isn't hard - I got one without taking physics in high school.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great! Cutoff for A is around 85. Exams are similar to practice exams so study those. Be careful tho bc one exam will be written by another prof, so harder. Does replace lowest with its average with final. Lots of hw which doesn't really help with exams, so do it for the grade. Lab was super easy. He recorded every single lecture and posted them.

the homework is very frustrating, but lab is easy, its actually quite helpful to go to recitation. physics is like notoriously hard but you just need to do alot of practice problems and the exams will go well. expect curveballs in the exams but a fair share of the class ends with an A >50%

Dr. Ford has great chapter notes in Canvas. Redo past exams and look over lecture notes to review for exams. This class is very exam-heavy. There is a lot of homework. Recitation is very helpful, so make sure to attend.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His lectures are hard to learn from. However, you can look at his chapter notes and read the textbook which will help you do the homework. Recitation is insanely helpful if you come prepared with questions from old exams. You basically just hard study the old exams as much as you can.

His lectures are very old school so it takes a good amount of self-learning. Homework is annoying. Just hard study the past exams and you will do decently good on the exams. His final will have the same problems from past exams, just take a good amount to go through those.

Ford is a very nice guy, but his lectures are very dry and he mumbles. He posts past year's exams which are good to study. I attended all of his lectures but I ultimately taught myself the material using the homework, old exams, and online textbook. Exams are really not that difficult, but are department-wide so this isn't unique to Ford.

This is a class that will make you study, but Ford is very accessible for questions. The homework is very difficult but the exams are easy so if you can do the homework the exams should not be a problem. Do homework early so you have time to ask questions at his review sessions before the exams. Sit near the front, he is quiet,

Best professor to take out of the other professors. Old-fashioned teaching style and sometimes mumbles during lectures. Goes over formulas and practice examples during lecture. Also posts recordings on Canvas. Skimming over his past notes before the lecture helps a lot. Exams are similar to past exams so study those. Homework is time-consuming.

Dr. Ford is very kind and provided all the resources students needed to get an A. There was a lot of Mastering Physics homework, but it was very helpful. The exams were worth a lot, but were not way too difficult after doing the practice exams and homework. Dr. Ford did practice problems in class and helped students a lot with homework questions.

Physics at TAMU is hard. Dr. Ford is your best option. Old fashioned teaching & never works through examples fully. Only shows general ideas, rarely solves problems with numbers. Practice exams are available that helped. Mastering Physics was a pain. Lab & recitation are grade boosters worth 12% of final grade. Got a 99 in lab &100 in recitation.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Ford is super nice and funny, but his teaching is very old-fashioned. I would say a majority of the class teaches themself the course. Don't be too intimidated. Try your best and your efforts will show. Focus more on practicing old exams rather than the homework because mastering physics questions are sometimes out of scope of the class.

I took from Wu for PHYS 201, and switched to Ford. I don't think it really matters who you take from, your best bet is going to be to teach yourself via the practice exams. Ford is good about answering questions over the homework and exams. He started doing pop quizzes to encourage attendance, and you get 40% for just showing up.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Physics is hard. I went in to the class intimidated, thinking I would be lucky to get a B. However, the lowest test grade I ever made was an 80. Ford gives several old practice exams for each test, and if you can solve those problems, you will do well on the exam. Heavy curves. Can be a little rude, but very open to questions during class.

Physics is so hard and I wish TAMU had some more solid profs to choose from. Ford is kind and generous however I never responded well to his lectures and never attended them after the first month of school. Whether I listened to lecture or not, my test grades remained the same and it was so difficult to learn the material!
Material is difficult, he does a good job of narrowing down what you need to know. has a ton of practice exams.

Honestly, this class was very doable because of the SI. I stopped going to class and just went to Andrew's sessions. If Andrew doesn't SI then go to A+. The best way to prepare for Ford's exams is to do his previous exams which he posts online. Ford is the best general physics prof at A&M because of his exams, not his teaching methods.

Phys is hard but Fords tests are very straight forward and he also gives you all of his pasts test from previous years which helps tremendously. Hes also just a really nice guy, couldnt recommend him more.

I gave up going to class halfway through the semester. I still pulled a 100% on every exam. I had a great SI leader, so I invested most of my studying time in the SI sessions. I also read the textbook through, though barely helped. The key to Ford is that he is very predictable, so just practice all his past exams since they are available online.

If you take College Physics at TAMU, you NEED Dr. Ford. Nobody else compares. Physics is tough. Period. But Dr. Ford is helpful and straightforward with his expectations and actually wants to help you. I had a really tough few weeks in the middle of the semester and he let me make up some homework that I missed. He is the most precious man ever

Physics 202 is a great class and Dr. Ford is an amazing professor who can teach the subject well. Tests are easy and are similar to old exams. Homework is time-consuming but very doable. Lab and recitation are super easy. Good and comprehendible lectures.

Dr. Ford is THE best physics professor at Texas A&M, just look at his gpa distributions. It is a very hard class, but Dr. Ford makes it very manageable for you to understand the topics and succeed. He is kinda confusing during lectures so outside tutoring will help tremendously. His tests are based on his previous tests, so just study old tests.

Dr. Ford is one of the best professors at A&M hands down. He comes off as a grumpy old man, but is so chill and one of the sweetest professors you will talk to. His class is 100% straightforward. 4 tests with mastering physics homework and the final can replace your lowest test grade. I am taking him again for physics 202. 10/10 recommend!

Dr. Ford is very consistent with his tests and they are fair. They are not usually too hard and they come from the old practice exams and relevant material that was covered in lecture. It also helps that lab and recitation count towards your average, so be sure to attend those and study for the quizzes. I strongly recommend him for physics.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I had ford for 201/202. Hes not a bad guy just the material for physics is EXTREMELY DIFFICULT(202 is even harder!) Im not kidding! Most students are taking other science classes, so be prepared to have a tough schedule if youre taking phys, ochem, bio etc. He tries to lecture and ask students q's in class but many didnt know the answers. Beware...
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Ford is a great professor. He is a fair grader and his exams arent too bad if you put in A LOT of time and effort into understanding the material. I made a B but an A is more than doable if you dont have a heavy semester while taking this class. Reaching out for help is key.

Dr. Ford is the most wonderful professor Ive had so far in college. He is so so so kind and goes out of his way to make sure we understand the material and have plenty of time to ask questions. He is always available, quick to respond to emails, fast test grader, and more than fair. That being said, physics is still really hard but TAKE HIM!!
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Nice older man. Occasional jokes in class. Best 201 prof fall 2017. Lecture helps w/ hw and test. Class has ONLINE hw (difficult w/out help. 8% of grade), lab (easy. 7% grade), + recitation (helpful. problems covered are usually on test. Easy quizzes worth 5% of grade). Must know trig and alg. Study for test by practicing old exams.

Dr. Ford is a great professor who teaches the material well! He cares about his students, and he is always available and helpful during office hours. However, the tests were written by four professors this year, and were pretty difficult and somewhat unfair on some of the questions. The curve overall in the class helps a lot though!

Ford goes over a TON of examples in class that help a lot with the material. If you can teach yourself through the material with the textbook, then go for it, but he makes it much more understandable and is always read to help. Also, his previous exams are very similar to the exam of that year, so definitely go through as many as you can.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is fair when writing the tests and really cares if we know the material. He'll get behind (but then catches up) on the syllabus schedule to answer questions about homework problems. The homework problems are way harder than the exam questions. If you go over previous exams, pay attention in class, and go to the SI sessions, you'll do fine.

Dr. Ford was a solid professor. Knows the material really well, taught it well, and is extremely helpful. His lectures are kind of old school but he does provide examples and past practice exams to study. Homework is difficult, lab and recitation are easy, and exams are pretty hard mainly because they're made by 4 professors and not only by Ford.

He provides a lot of ways to review for each test, but there is a lot of homework with each test. He is very old school and does not use many online resources or post grades on ecampus. But there is a website with all of his previous exams along with the correct answers. The lab portion and recitation are easy As.
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: I've always hated physics and been really bad at it. But Ford is a great professor. He lets you know what exactly you need to know for each unit and gives you lots of opportunities to ask questions. He also has a BUNCH of his old tests from previous years online for you to practice. Great prof and a really nice guy :)

Dr Ford is the best physics professor you can take for 201. He really cares about his students and will answer a ton of homework questions in class. The homework load is heavy but the tests are far easier than the homework, which is helpful. Go over old tests to study for upcoming ones, they're often very similar. He writes the tests too!

There's a lot of homework, and it's physics so of course it will be difficult, but Dr. Ford teaches it well. He teaches the concepts behind the math and then goes through practice problems. You don't have to go to class if you can learn it on your won, but it's helpful to. He's funny and respectful.

I don't really like physics, and I'm not naturally good at it, but I was able to learn the material from Dr. Ford well.  He works examples-very helpful.  Do the homework, similar questions on test.  Also use practice exams.  Doing that, you can make an A.
